name: Yves-Loic Martin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Yves-Loic Martin is the former chief technology officer of Eurofins Scientific, a  laboratory testing company listed on the French stock exchange.
Martin owns about 10% of the company, which went public in 1997.
He joined Eurofins in 1992 and became chief technology officer in 1998. He stepped down in 2015 but remains a board member.
Eurofins has 400 labs in 41 countries and is prominent in food and pharmaceutical products testing.
Martin's billionaire brother, Gilles, founded the lab in 1987 and remains CEO.

name: Robert Fisher
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Robert "Bob" Fisher is one of three sons of Gap founders Donald (d. 2009) and Doris Fisher.
He is managing director of the Fisher family's investment firm, Pisces, and chaired Gap's board until 2020.
Like his two billionaire brothers, he attended Princeton, where he played tennis and majored in English, before heading to Stanford's business school.
A philanthropist, Fisher cofounded the California Water Foundation, which focuses on improving California's water supply, in 2010.

name: Xue Jiping
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2025); Hurun China (2007-2024)
forbes_bio: Xue Jiping is the founder of Jiangsu Zhongtian Technology, a supplier of optical fiber communication products. He stepped down as chairman in June 2025 and handed over leadership to his son, Xue Chi.
Zhongtian's predecessor business was a small collective factory that made bricks and tiles.
ZTT Group, Xue's listed arm, entered the field of optical fiber communication in the early 1990s.
ZTT went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange on Oct 24, 2002.

name: Tibor Veres
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Veres Tibor is one of Hungary's most reclusive business leaders.
Through holding companies, he controls interests in automobiles, real estate development, retail and manufacturing.
Founded in 1987 Wallis Group operates in real estate development, automotive, retail, logistics and manufacturing.
Wallis's Dayton-Invest is majority owner of WING, a real estate business with interests in Hungary, Poland and Germany.
Veres also controls AutoWallis, a leading automotive and mobility service provider 23 brands operating across Central and Eastern Europe.
forbes_facts: He graduated from the University of Moscow in 1986 and returned to Hungary where he founded Wallis Group with his father and another co-founder.
Veres is a member of the UNICEF Hungary Board of Trustees.

name: Victoria Goh
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Victoria Goh is a granddaughter of the late Singaporean paints tycoon Goh Cheng Liang, who died in August 2025 at age 98.
The Goh family draws the bulk of its wealth from a majority stake in Japan's Nippon Paint Holdings, one of the world's largest paint manufacturers.
Victoria, together with her two sisters and three cousins, inherited the bulk of their grandfather's fortune.
Her father is Hup Jin, the eldest child of the late patriarch who started making paints in a small factory in Singapore before partnering with Nippon Paint in 1962.
Hup Jin is the chairman of Nippon Paint.

name: Chen Shibin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Shibin chairs Jiangsu Pacific Quartz, a supplier of quartz material for the lighting and solar industries.
Pacific Quartz went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2014.
Pacific Quartz is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Lianyungang.

name: Stewart Butterfield
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Stewart Butterfield is the cofounder and former CEO of team-based messaging software Slack.
In 2021, cloud software giant Salesforce acquired Slack for $27.7 billion in cash and stock.
Butterfield departed Salesforce in 2022, amid an exodus of executives at the company.
Butterfield and wife Jen Rubio, the founder of luggage startup Away, sold their San Francisco home and moved to Aspen in 2020.
Though he cofounded a tech company, Butterfield proudly majored in philosophy as an undergraduate at Canada's University of Victoria.
forbes_facts: Butterfield cofounded image hosting site Flickr in 2003; it was purchased by Yahoo for $35 million in 2005.

appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: Lou Guoqiang derives his fortune from Ningbo Jintian Copper, a supplier of copper rod and other copper products.
Lou formerly chaired the company before his son Lou Cheng took over the role in 2022.
The company, which was founded in 1986, provides integrated copper solutions for rail transit, power IoT and smart-city development. Its business spans more than 100 countries and regions.

name: Li Haiyan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026); Hurun China (2018-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2018-2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Li Haiyan is a co-founder of  hot-pot chain Haidilao International Holdings; she has been a company supervisor since 2009.
Li is the wife of billionaire Shi Yonghong, a director at Haidilao and chairman of  hotpot seasonings supplier Yihai International.
Haidilao co-founders Li, Zhang Yong, Shu Ping and Shi Yonghong funded their first restaurant with personal savings in 1994.
Haidilao today is one of the most popular restaurant chains in China and has about 1,300 locations worldwide.

name: Jeff Sprecher
sec_insider_companies: Intercontinental Exchange, Inc. (ICE) - Chief Executive Officer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Jeff Sprecher is the founder and CEO of global stock exchange operator Intercontinental Exchange, also known as ICE.
In 1997, Sprecher was working at a California power plant developer when he negotiated to buy a struggling Georgia company called Continental Power Exchange.
He had an idea to create a platform that would allow traders to buy and sell commodities online.
In 2000, Sprecher folded Continental into new firm ICE; he took that company public in 2005.
In 2013, ICE acquired the New York Stock Exchange for $10.9 billion; it owns 12 stock exchanges and 6 clearing houses globally.
forbes_facts: Sprecher is married to Kelly Loeffler, who was appointed U.S. Senator from Georgia in 2019 to fill an empty seat; she lost the special election in January 2021.

name: Werner O. Weber
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2021-2024); Hurun Global (2022-2025)
forbes_bio: Werner O. Weber holds around half of publicly traded LEM, a Swiss manufacturer of current and voltage transducers that measure electricity.
Founded in 1972, LEM has been listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange since 1986.
It has production plants in Beijing, China; Geneva, Switzerland; Machida, Japan, and Sofia, Bulgaria.
Weber also has a sizable stake in Zug Estates Holding, a Swiss real estate developer.
The rest of his portfolio includes a Swiss medical device maker, a home goods manufacturer and an automated technology producer.
